messages.subject: Linux and TMB
messages.body_plain:
Hi all.

I am contemplating using Linux as my operating system to facilitate TMB, ADMB and R analyses.  I have an old Win 7 system and am thinking of uninstalling that operating system and replacing it with Linux of which there are a number of variants (Ubuntu, Mint, Fedora, etc etc).

Does anyone have experience with TMB and ADMB in Linux and if so, do you have any recommendations re the best Linux variant for TMB, ADMB, R etc analyses, installation heads up and so on?

Any thoughts on this are much appreciated.

Bob

messages.body_plain:
If you want something that works straight out of the box I probably would suggest ubuntu.   Personally I normally use debian,  but that is because I am a weirdo.  I think finding a text editor that you love, and a terminal that works for you, are more important than the distro.

messages.subject: Re: [TMB users] Linux and TMB
messages.body_plain:
I've been using Mint for about 10 years (it's OK, currently v19.2), the
Gnome terminal that comes with the distro (tweak the colors and fonts a
bit), gvim (most people hate vi, but I can't help myself), Gnu C++ (and
clang just to keep the compilers honest), compile R from source (with
shared libraries enabled), Python 3 (for those times when R just doesn't
cut it).

Others would make different choices; web is full of (mostly BS) opinions
about what is the best distrol. The answer is the best one is the one
that seems to fit your mode of work.

John
